newsitem.title: CUBA: French businessman sees Cuba opportunities.
newsitem.headline: French businessman sees Cuba opportunities.

text.p: The leader of a French business delegation visiting Cuba said on Saturday the U.S. embargo against the island created good opportunities there for French companies because U.S. competition was absent.
"The fact that Cuba is under embargo is a very good opportunity," Gerard Bourgoin, founder of the French poultry group Bourgoin S.A., told a news conference in Havana.
Washington's 35-year-old economic embargo against communist-ruled Cuba prevents U.S. companies from doing business there.
Bourgoin, president of a new business organization, the Federation of Enterprises and Entrepreneurs of France (FEEF), brought about 60 French executives with him.

During a four-day visit this week, the group met Cuban President Fidel Castro and Vice President Carlos Lage, held talks with government ministers and visited biotechnology centers, a tobacco farm and a cigar factory.
"It's a 100 percent business trip, with no political nuances," Bourgoin said.

Of the delegation members, "some 15 or so have already fixed up meetings to return (to Cuba) with business proposals or projects," he said. He mentioned the food industry, metallurgy and tourism as areas of opportunity.
The Bourgoin group exports around 8,000 tonnes of poultry meat to Cuba each year.

Bourgoin said he was also president of a Montreal-based Canadian company, Pebercam, which is prospecting for oil in six onshore Cuban exploration blocks. The company had prepared a program of 15 exploration wells, he said. The first was scheduled to be drilled at the end of February.
On the U.S. Helms-Burton law, which seeks to deter foreign investment in Cuba, Bourgoin said: "You have to work with it."

He said the six Cuban oil blocks where Pebercam was working were free from claims under Helms-Burton. The law threatens to penalize foreign firms judged to be "trafficking" in expropriated, formerly U.S.-owned properties on the island.
